title: What Is Corgi Insurance? Startup Cover, Funding and Valuation
seo_title: What Is Corgi Insurance? Cover, Funding and Valuation
meta: What is Corgi insurance? An AI-native insurer for startups that raised a $160M Series B and a $106M B1 in 2026. What it sells and how the valuations line up.
dek: Corgi is an AI-native insurance platform for startups founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua. This covers what it sells, how it raised money in 2026 and how the valuations line up.
intent: Informational and news: what is Corgi insurance, who runs it, how much is it worth.
questions: Why do two valuations appear in the news?

needs: Confirm which valuation applies to which round (reports differ: US$1.3B at Series B, US$2.6B at B1).
body:
Corgi is an insurance company built for startups, founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua, which emerged from stealth in January 2026 and raised a US$160 million Series B in May 2026 at a reported US$1.3 billion valuation, led by TCV. A further US$106 million B1 round in June was reported at US$2.6 billion.

What it sells

Corgi offers general liability, cyber liability and technology and AI liability cover, with instant quotes and modular policies matched to a startup's stage. The company calls itself full-stack because it is building the insurance carrier and the software that prices policies rather than reselling other insurers' products.

How the funding adds up

  1. January 2026: US$108 million of combined seed and Series A, co-led by Y Combinator and Kindred Ventures.
  2. May 2026: US$160 million Series B led by TCV, bringing total funding past US$268 million at a reported US$1.3 billion valuation.
  3. June 2026: US$106 million Series B1, also led by TCV, reported at a US$2.6 billion valuation.

The two valuations are not a contradiction: they are different rounds three weeks apart.

Where it is going

Company announcements say it will expand beyond startup insurance into trucking, payroll and small business.

A note on caution

Insurance is regulated by state, and a young carrier has a short claims history. Anyone buying cover should check the carrier's licence and the policy's exclusions.
